2  	title: use cache
3  	description: Learn how to use the "use cache" directive to cache data in your Next.js application.
4  	related:
5  	  title: Related
6  	  description: View related API references.
7  	  links:
8  	    - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private
9  	    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents
10 	    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife
11 	    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheHandlers

13 	    - app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife

15 	---
16 	
17 	The `use cache` directive allows you to mark a route, React component, or a function as cacheable. It can be used at the top of a file to indicate that all exports in the file should be cached, or inline at the top of a function or component to cache the return value. Functions and components that use `use cache` must be async.
18 	
19 	> **Good to know:**
20 	>
21 	> - To use cookies or headers, read them outside cached scopes and pass values as arguments. This is the preferred pattern.
22 	> - If the in-memory cache isn't sufficient for runtime data, [`'use cache: remote'`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote) allows platforms to provide a dedicated cache handler, though it requires a network roundtrip to check the cache and typically incurs platform fees.
23 	> - For compliance requirements or when you can't refactor to pass runtime data as arguments to a `use cache` scope, see [`'use cache: private'`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private).
24 	
25 	## Usage
26 	
27 	`use cache` is a Cache Components feature. To enable it, add the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) option to your `next.config.ts` file:
28 	
29 	```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
30 	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
31 	
32 	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
33 	  cacheComponents: true,
34 	}
35 	
36 	export default nextConfig
37 	```
38 	
39 	```js filename="next.config.js" switcher
40 	/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
41 	const nextConfig = {
42 	  cacheComponents: true,
43 	}
44 	
45 	module.exports = nextConfig
46 	```
47 	
48 	Then, add `use cache` at the function, component, or file level. Cached functions and components must be async:
49 	
50 	```tsx
51 	// Function level
52 	export async function getData() {
53 	  'use cache'
54 	  const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data')
55 	  const data = await res.json()
56 	  return data
57 	}
58 	
59 	// Component level
60 	export async function MyComponent() {
61 	  'use cache'
62 	  return <></>
63 	}
64 	```
65 	
66 	When used at file level, every exported function becomes a cached function and must also be async:
67 	
68 	```tsx
69 	// File level
70 	'use cache'
71 	
72 	export default async function Page() {
73 	  // ...
74 	}
75 	```
76 	
77 	## How `use cache` works
78 	
79 	### Cache keys
80 	
81 	A cache entry's key is generated using a serialized version of its inputs, which includes:
82 	
83 	1. **Build ID** - Unique per build, changing this invalidates all cache entries. If [`deploymentId`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/deploymentId) is configured, it overrides the build ID for cache key purposes.
84 	2. **Function ID** - A secure hash of the function's location and signature in the codebase
85 	3. **Serializable arguments** - Props (for components) or function arguments
86 	4. **HMR refresh hash** (development only) - Invalidates cache on hot module replacement
87 	
88 	When a cached function references variables from outer scopes, those variables are automatically captured and bound as arguments, making them part of the cache key.
89 	
90 	```tsx filename="lib/data.ts"
91 	async function Component({ userId }: { userId: string }) {
92 	  const getData = async (filter: string) => {
93 	    'use cache'
94 	    // Cache key includes both userId (from closure) and filter (argument)
95 	    const res = await fetch(
96 	      `https://api.example.com/users/${userId}/data?filter=${filter}`
97 	    )
98 	    return res.json()
99 	  }
100	
101	  return getData('active')
102	}
103	```
104	
105	In the snippet above, `userId` is captured from the outer scope and `filter` is passed as an argument, so both become part of the `getData` function's cache key. This means different user and filter combinations will have separate cache entries.
106	
107	> **Good to know:** When a cached function reads [root parameters](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-root-params), only the ones it actually reads become part of its cache key.
108	
109	### Cache output
110	
111	A cached function produces the same output for the same inputs. The first call with a given set of inputs runs the function body and stores its output. Every later call with the same inputs reuses that output, within a render pass and across requests, for as long as the entry lasts.
112	
113	Outputs are stored by a [cache handler](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheHandlers), [in memory](#runtime-caching-considerations) by default, and last until they [revalidate](#revalidation).
114	
115	```tsx filename="lib/orders.ts"
116	import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache'
117	
118	export async function getOrderSummary(accountId: string) {
119	  'use cache'
120	  cacheLife('hours')
121	
122	  const orders = await getOrders(accountId)
123	  const totals = await getOrderTotals(accountId)
124	
125	  return { orders, totals }
126	}
127	
128	export async function getOrders(accountId: string) {
129	  'use cache'
130	  cacheLife('hours')
131	
132	  return db.orders.findMany({ where: { accountId } })
133	}
134	
135	export async function getOrderTotals(accountId: string) {
136	  return db.orders.aggregate({ where: { accountId }, _sum: { amount: true } })
137	}
138	```
139	
140	In the example above, each `accountId` has its own entry for `getOrderSummary`, holding the serialized `{ orders, totals }` object it returns. Calls to `getOrders` have their own entries, keyed by the same `accountId`. If an earlier call, through the summary or directly, already filled one, `db.orders.findMany` doesn't run and those orders become part of the summary's output. See [nested caching behavior](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#nested-caching-behavior) for how an inner lifetime affects the entry around it.
141	
142	Note that `getOrderTotals` is not cached. It is exported so other parts of the application can read fresh totals in an uncached scope. Inside `getOrderSummary`, though, the totals query only runs when that function runs following the `'hours'` lifetime set there.
143	
144	With [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), prerendering fills the entry and keeps rendering, so this output contributes to the route's [static shell](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#prerendering) and can contribute to its [prefetch](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#prefetching). A cache life too short to store safely leaves a hole that resolves at request time instead. See [prerendering behavior](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#prerendering-behavior) for the thresholds.
145	
146	## Serialization
147	
148	Arguments to cached functions and their return values must be serializable.
149	
150	For a complete reference, see:
151	
152	- [Serializable arguments](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-server#serializable-parameters-and-return-values) - Uses **React Server Components** serialization
153	- [Serializable return types](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-client#serializable-types) - Uses **React Client Components** serialization
154	
155	> **Good to know:** Arguments and return values use different serialization systems. Server Component serialization (for arguments) is more restrictive than Client Component serialization (for return values). This means you can return JSX elements but cannot accept them as arguments unless using pass-through patterns.
156	
157	### Supported types
158	
159	**Arguments:**
160

See [preset cache profiles](#preset-cache-profiles) for timing details. 84 85 ## Reference 86 87 ### Cache profile properties 88 89 Cache profiles control caching behavior through three timing properties: 90 91 - **[`stale`](#stale)**: How long the client can use cached data without checking the server 92 - **[`revalidate`](#revalidate)**: After this time, the next request will trigger a background refresh 93 - **[`expire`](#expire)**: After this time with no requests, the next one waits for fresh content 94 95 #### `stale` 96 97 **Client-side:** How long the client can use cached data without checking the server. 98 99 During this time, the client-side router displays cached content immediately without any network request. After this period expires, the router must check with the server on the next navigation or request. This provides instant page loads from the client cache, but data may be outdated. 100 101 - If omitted, defaults to the `default` profile's `stale` value (5 minutes, see [`staleTimes`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/staleTimes)) 102 - Also determines whether the content can be part of the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). 1  	---
2  	title: cacheTag
3  	description: Learn how to use the cacheTag function to manage cache invalidation in your Next.js application.
4  	related:
5  	  title: Related
6  	  description: View related API references.
7  	  links:
8  	    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents
9  	    - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache
10 	    - app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag

13 	---
14 	
15 	The `cacheTag` function allows you to tag cached data for on-demand invalidation. By associating tags with cache entries, you can selectively purge or revalidate specific cache entries without affecting other cached data.
16 	
17 	## Usage
18 	
19 	To use `cacheTag`, enable the [`cacheComponents` flag](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.js` file:
20 	
21 	```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
22 	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
23 	
24 	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
25 	  cacheComponents: true,
26 	}
27 	
28 	export default nextConfig
29 	```
30 	
31 	```js filename="next.config.js" switcher
32 	const nextConfig = {
33 	  cacheComponents: true,
34 	}
35 	
36 	module.exports = nextConfig
37 	```
38 	
39 	The `cacheTag` function takes one or more string values.
40 	
41 	```tsx filename="app/data.ts" switcher
42 	import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
43 	
44 	export async function getData() {
45 	  'use cache'
46 	  cacheTag('my-data')
47 	  const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data')
48 	  const data = await res.json()
49 	  return data
50 	}
51 	```
52 	
53 	```jsx filename="app/data.js" switcher
54 	import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
55 	
56 	export async function getData() {
57 	  'use cache'
58 	  cacheTag('my-data')
59 	  const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data')
60 	  const data = await res.json()
61 	  return data
62 	}
63 	```
64 	
65 	You can then purge the cache on-demand from a [Server Function](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route):
66 	
67 	- Use [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) for read-your-own-writes scenarios, such as forms and other user-triggered mutations, where a user makes a change and the next read should fetch fresh data immediately. `updateTag` is only available inside Server Functions.
68 	- Use [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) when it is acceptable to serve stale data while revalidation happens in the background, or when revalidating from a [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) or other context.
69 	
70 	For example, this Server Function adds a post and then purges every cache entry tagged `'my-data'` so the next read reflects the change:
71 	
72 	```tsx filename="app/action.ts" switcher
73 	'use server'
74 	
75 	import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
76 	
77 	export default async function submit() {
78 	  await addPost()
79 	  updateTag('my-data')
80 	}
81 	```
82 	
83 	```jsx filename="app/action.js" switcher
84 	'use server'
85 	
86 	import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
87 	
88 	export default async function submit() {
89 	  await addPost()
90 	  updateTag('my-data')
91 	}
92 	```
93 	
94 	## Good to know
95 	
96 	- **Idempotent Tags**: Applying the same tag multiple times has no additional effect.
97 	- **Multiple Tags**: You can assign multiple tags to a single cache entry by passing multiple string values to `cacheTag`.
98 	
99 	```tsx

1 	---
2 	title: cacheComponents
3 	description: Learn how to enable the cacheComponents flag in Next.js.
4 	related:
5 	  links:
6 	    - app/getting-started/caching
7 	    - app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components
8 	    - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache
9 	    - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote
10	---
11	
12	Cache Components enables component and function-level caching using the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive. Data fetching is dynamic by default, and you choose what to cache at the page, component, or function level. Next.js prerenders a static HTML shell that is served immediately while dynamic content streams in when ready, letting you mix static and dynamic content within a single route.
13	
14	## Usage
15	
16	To enable the `cacheComponents` flag, set it to `true` in your `next.config.ts` file:
17	
18	```ts filename="next.config.ts"
19	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
20	
21	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
22	  cacheComponents: true,
23	}
24	
25	export default nextConfig
26	```
27	
28	> **Good to know**: Cache Components requires the Node.js runtime. Migrate any routes that set the deprecated `runtime = 'edge'` export, and note that other server-side JavaScript runtimes are not guaranteed to work. See [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components#runtime--edge).
29	
30	When `cacheComponents` is enabled, you can use the following cache functions and configurations:
31	
32	- The [`use cache` directive](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache)
33	- The [`cacheLife` function](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife) with `use cache`
34	- The [`cacheTag` function](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag)
35	
36	> **Good to know**: If you used `experimental.useCache` or `experimental.dynamicIO`, migrate using the [Version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#experimentaldynamicio-and-experimentalusecache). To migrate route segment configs and other caching patterns, see [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components).
37	
38	Additionally, `cacheComponents` implements **[Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prerendering-ppr)** as the default behavior in the App Router. This means the `experimental.ppr` configuration flag and the `experimental_ppr` route segment configuration are no longer necessary and have been removed.
39	
40	Read [Prerendering](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#prerendering) for how the static shell and streaming fit together.
41	
42	> **Good to know**: If you used experimental PPR in Next.js 15, refer to the [Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#partial-prerendering-ppr) section of the Version 16 upgrade guide when migrating.
43	
44	## Navigation with Activity
45	
46	When `cacheComponents` is enabled, Next.js uses React's [`<Activity>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity) component to preserve component state during client-side navigation.
47	
48	Rather than unmounting the previous route when you navigate away, Next.js sets the Activity mode to [`"hidden"`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity#activity). This means:
49	
50	- Component state is preserved when navigating between routes
51	- When you navigate back, the previous route reappears with its state intact
52	- Effects are cleaned up when a route is hidden, and recreated when it becomes visible again
53	
54	This behavior improves the navigation experience by maintaining UI state (form inputs, or expanded sections) when users navigate back and forth between routes.
55	
56	> **Good to know**: Next.js uses heuristics to keep a few recently visited routes `"hidden"`, while older routes are removed from the DOM to prevent excessive growth.
57	
58	Some UI patterns behave differently when components stay mounted instead of unmounting. See the [Preserving UI state guide](/docs/app/guides/preserving-ui-state) for handling common patterns like dropdowns, dialogs, and testing.
59	
60	## Version History
61	
62	| Version | Change                                                                                                                            |
63	| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
64	| 16.0.0  | `cacheComponents` introduced. This flag controls the `ppr`, `useCache`, and `dynamicIO` flags as a single, unified configuration. |
</content>
